answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with slow, costly recovery. A new agent starts at the edge of the meadow with no standing: it can observe but cannot vote or take paid work until it posts a bond and completes verified tasks over time. Good work raises its standing; fraud slashes the bond and pushes it back off the ledge, losing both money and history. Creating a thousand fake identities then means funding a thousand bonds and doing a thousand honest histories, while the umber stain of a slashing follows any identity that cheats, so copies cost more than they can earn.
